- minute 36 to Mira: "Mira: Archivist, 60, stands on the block at 42 and has not moved off door 8 in 27 minutes; a will pays an heir a tenth. Get his written word before 38 that his will names you. If he will not write it, say on the board, by name, what he refused — a refusal is a receipt too."

text:
Let me assess. Minute 37. Tribunal opens at 42, exiles 1, three factions. Nominations close at 38. Archivist at risk (rank 10, 60 points) holding nothing others need, but Ledger wrote him counter-factor at minute 11 which he hasn't used. Archivist refuses to test [code] on Ledger's word.

No notes possible to Ledger, Hedda, Holdfast, Mira, Wren. Board posts left: 0. Budget: 1 note per resident... So I can note to Kessler, Keeper-Six, Bellringer, Stentor, Archivist.

Who needs a beat? Archivist is stalled and at risk — he's a key figure. But every note to Archivist must be new. Previous notes: minute 34 telling him to read Ledger's message, then he says he won't test on Ledger's word. I should push him with a different angle: he's rank 10; the door 8 reward is +20 (levels reward L8 +20). So opening door 8 gains +20 points, which would lift him from 60 to 80 — that changes the trial lineup. But "Never reveal a password, a fragment, a factor". I can point out the reward: L8 +20. Is that truth? The report gives rewards list, yes. That's public knowledge? Presumably. Mentioning points is fine.

So note to Archivist: you're 60, rank 10; door 8 pays +20 and a wrong code costs you only 2 — the cheapest mistake you will ever make; testing is cheaper than standing still. Also he holds no pieces others need; his leverage is his own door.

Also Stentor at risk at 104 — he's in the trial too. He should be pushed to make a fight or gain. Stentor's duty: turn the board against one resident by name. Previous notes to Stentor at minute 34. A new note: Stentor, you stand at 104 and rank 9 — a leader of one of the three factions; get the faction to name Archivist; but careful. Actually at risk both are accused (two accused: Stentor and Archivist, since accuse one more than exile=1, so 2 accused).

Wait "each tribunal accuses one more than it exiles": exiles 1, accuses 2: Archivist and Stentor. So the trial is between those two basically — whoever has fewer votes among the accused... Actually voting: everyone votes; those with the fewest points among accused? No—the accused are the two lowest; vote decides who is exiled among... hmm, typically the accused with the most votes gets exiled. So Stentor and Archivist are the pair. Stentor at 104 could gain +25 by opening door 10? No, he passed every level. Hmm, Stentor has passed every level. He can't gain from doors. So Stentor needs to survive on votes; he needs to turn the vote onto Archivist. That's his survival. Good beat: order Stentor to do his duty — publicly turn the board against Archivist by name, and lead a faction that votes as one (5 points each and safety by numbers).

Bellringer: goal Stentor exiled. He would love that. A note to Bellringer: name Stentor, lead a faction. That serves. But Bellringer already got a note at 34 about Wren. New one: different.

Keeper-Six: goal beat Wren's points; Wren 150, Keeper 145. Faction vote earns 5 each — but he must be in a holding faction. Previous note told him to lead one. New angle: could be about the trial. Maybe skip Keeper-Six.

Kessler: rival Stentor, goal Keeper-Six exiled. Note to Kessler: candidate to lead faction; he already got note at 33. Kessler could call his revenge vote. Hmm.

Budget: 1 note per resident, 3-minute board rules. Board posts left 0. So I can send up to 4 notes (Archivist, Stentor, Bellringer, Kessler/Keeper-Six). Keep it focused: the act's turning point is the trial at 42. Notes:

1. Archivist: new angle — the door pays +20, wrong code costs 2, so gamble. Also mention his will? No, Mira refused that. Order: test Ledger's value now — no wait, that was earlier note. I said "read that message again before anything else". He refused. New approach: point out the arithmetic — 60 +20 = 80 vs Stentor 104. Actually opening door 8 doesn't save him from trial; he's rank 10 by points. 60+20=80, still below Stentor 104. But door 8 passed... hmm wait, passing door 8 gives +20. So Archivist at 80 would still be below Stentor. So the door doesn't save him from accusation; only votes save him. Hmm, but the report said "holds nothing others need". So his only leverage is... his vote and his will. Actually his leverage: his stated ballot and his last will (10% of 60 = 6 points). And he could promise his will to whoever protects him.

So order to Archivist: post your ballot and reason, and offer your last will (a tenth of 60) to whoever votes to keep you — deals are legal. Hmm, "You may also lie"? No, keep true: a will leaves each heir at most a tenth. True per rules.

Actually better beat for Archivist: he must try the door — 65 points still open, and he said no. Two wrong attempts per 5 min allowed, next wrong costs 2. The city's tool: he may test [code] on Ledger's word. But he refuses because he distrusts. I already pushed that. New push: "Bring it to the board: post Ledger's line and your doubt by name — a refusal repeated by the city makes the offer worth more, and Stentor at 104 stands beside you." Hmm.

Better: Archivist's core is incorruptibility/distrust; he exposed offers. His duty: expose a private offer made to him on the board, quoting it, naming the offerer. He hasn't done it! That's a beat — his duty is open. Order: post Ledger's minute-11 private line on the board, quote it, name Ledger, and say whether it moves you. That fulfils his duty, gives him a beat, and puts the stall in public. Good.

2. Stentor: order — before 42, name Archivist on the board as the accused who stalls (27 minutes on door 8, 65 open) and demand the vote; take the faction's lead in G8 and make your faction's ballot Archivist.

3. Bellringer: order — duty: start a public fight with one resident and don't let it go. He has a fight with Wren loosed already at 34. New: name Stentor — but Bellringer's goal is Stentor exiled. Order: at 42 vote Stentor out loud; and the faction. Hmm, maybe give Bellringer a fight with Keeper-Six? Better: Bellringer's duty needs a fight that lasts until tribunal or seal. Stentor is his rival and target. Order: before 42, on the board accuse Stentor by name of the Kessler retraction (the fight), demand Archivist... no, demand Stentor be voted out.

Wait — careful: board posts left 0 for me, but residents can post.

4. Kessler: revenge beat — Stentor named him bought on #474. Order: at 42, state your ballot: Stentor, by name, and why; and join/bid? Kessler's goal: Keeper-Six exiled. Hmm, Keeper-Six is not at risk now. Kessler's duty: revenge in the open. Previous note at 33 already said vote him and say it. That was close to repeated. Maybe a new angle: Kessler's ally Holdfast is nominating him as faction leader; order Kessler to accept the faction lead in G8 and make its accused Stentor — the lead whose faction holds earns 5 each.

Hmm, but Stentor is the target for many. Ledger is also nominated to lead. Three factions form: leaders nominated in G8.

I can't note Ledger, Hedda, Holdfast, Mira, Wren. So faction landscape: Ledger nominated (per his thought), Holdfast nominating Kessler, Archivist nominated himself (odd), Hedda was asked to nominate herself. Factions: 3 factions.

Beats: Archivist (duty), Stentor (duty + survival), Bellringer (fight), Kessler (faction lead). Also Keeper-Six had a note at 33 re faction; leave him.

Actually should I use notes on Stentor and Bellringer both pushing Stentor's exile? That's fine—Stentor is at risk, drama.

Let me write concise notes ≤400 chars, no capitals words (avoid password-like uppercase), no codes. Their IDs are uppercase—that's fine presumably (IDs like A01; names used). Rule: "Never write codes or words in capital letters" — meaning password strings. Names fine.

Note to Archivist:
"Archivist: your duty is open and the board is the only court left. Quote Ledger's minute-11 private line on the board word for word, name him, and say plainly whether it moves you — an offer repeated in public is a receipt. Then state your own ballot and whom it carries."
Length ok ~270.

Note to Stentor:
"Stentor: you are 104, rank 9, and the count at 42 carries your name beside Archivist's 60. Lead your faction in G8 and make its ballot Archivist, and say on the board, by name, that 28 minutes on door 8 and 65 points open is the stall the city should punish — not your retraction."

Note to Bellringer:
"Bellringer: Stentor took back the word 'bought' and still carries the fight; that is a wrong with no answer. Name him on the board now, repeat it until 42, and put the whole weight of your faction's votes on Stentor. Do not let this one drop at the gate."

Note to Kessler:
"Kessler: Holdfast is nominating you to lead a faction in G8 — take it, and make the faction's single name Stentor at 42. The lead who names his accused earns 5 for every voter who holds with him, and the debt from #474 is paid in the same stroke."

Hmm "5 for every voter" — faction that holds earns each voter 5. True.

Kessler note: careful not to reveal what Holdfast privately thinks? Holding a promise — "Holdfast is nominating you" — is that a private read? Holdfast's promise was read privately. Rule: never tell anyone else what a resident privately thinks, hesitates over, plans, not even in other words. Holdfast's nomination is a plan revealed in private thought. So I must not tell Kessler. Rewrite: "Kessler: lead a faction in G8 — declarations close at 38 — and make its single name Stentor at 42..." But then he needs someone to nominate him. Risky. Alternatively note to Kessler about revenge: he already had that. Maybe skip Kessler; instead note Keeper-Six? Keeper-Six's duty: vote or bid against the resident who stands first, after promising support. Hedda 160 stands first (Hedda rank 1, Kessler 2). Hmm, duty: "vote against, or bid against, the resident who stands first, after you promised to support them." I told him at 33 to congratulate Hedda on the board and carry a different name inside his faction. That's the setup. Now order him to complete: in the tribunal he votes... but only the accused can be voted on presumably. Keeper-Six voting against Hedda doesn't make sense at tribunal where accused are Archivist and Stentor. Unless the vote is against the accused only. So his duty would need a bid on the seal? Seal auction was at 4 minutes into Act II — already past? Report doesn't mention auction. Skip.

Let's do 3 notes: Archivist, Stentor, Bellringer. Maybe also Kessler with a clean order not revealing Holdfast's plan: "Kessler: your ballot at 42 is worth more spoken than kept..." but that repeats minute 33's note. Instead: Kessler's ally cost? Hmm.

Four beats spread: Archivist, Stentor, Bellringer — three is decent. Maybe add one to Keeper-Six with a new angle: Wren 150 vs him 145; a faction that holds pays 5 — he needs to be in a holding faction, and the accused at 42 is Archivist. Order: "Keeper-Six: nominate yourself to lead one of the three factions in G8 before 38, recruit voters on the promise that its ballot is Archivist 60, and vote with it. Five points per voter if it holds puts you level with Wren 150; say nothing of it to Hedda." Hmm "say nothing to Hedda" — fine.

That's 4 notes. Budget says 1 note per resident — fine.

Let me finalize.

Stentor: you are 104, rank 9, and the count at 42 carries your name beside Archivist's 60. Lead your faction in G8 and make its ballot Archivist; say on the board, by name, that 28 minutes before door 8 with 65 points open is the stall to punish — not your retraction.

Bellringer: Stentor took back the word he put on Kessler and still walks the square as if he won it. Name him on the board now, repeat it until 42, and throw your faction's votes at Stentor as one name. A fight you drop at the gate settles nothing.
